punchline: Goleman says part of a signal reaches the amygdala before the thinking brain has caught up, which is why a reaction can beat reasoning.
thirty_sec: Daniel Goleman, a New York Times science reporter, built on Joseph LeDoux's work: a signal from the senses splits, one branch going straight to the amygdala and the other to the thinking brain. So a reaction can start first. He called it emotional hijacking, and argued IQ explains at most about a fifth of success. The book is Emotional Intelligence.
